stem:
Falguni has a paper cut-out of a capital letter $N$. She wants to decide whether it has line symmetry and whether it has rotational symmetry.

Which plan is correct?

options.text: Apply the fold test for line symmetry and the turn test for rotational symmetry as separate checks.
Answer rotational symmetry alone, naming that label instead of running both tests.
Decide from a single glance that whatever is true of one kind of symmetry is automatically true of the other.
Decide only from the bold printed letter $N$ on the worksheet title.

teacher.key_rationale: Fold and turn tests settle the two kinds independently for N. Naming one label alone substitutes a term. Treating one glance as both omits the separate-test condition. Using the printed title letter is surface capture.
